question: A 46-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination after a Pap smear showed atypical squamous cells. A colposcopy-directed biopsy of the cervix shows evidence of squamous cell carcinoma. The malignant cells from this lesion are most likely to drain into which of the following group of lymph nodes?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Squamous cell carcinoma in the cervix" -> "Lymphatic drainage from the cervix" -> "Superficial inguinal lymph nodes" -> 90%
enhanced_information: Squamous cell carcinoma in the cervix is most likely to drain into the superficial inguinal lymph nodes based on standard lymphatic drainage patterns. The evidence path supports the concept of lymphatic drainage from the cervix, aligning with this consensus.
analysis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix is most likely to drain into the superficial inguinal lymph nodes based on standard lymphatic drainage patterns.
